about.beginner: SovRing-Labs is one person's open research lab building AI that runs on the computers people already own. Its core idea is the residue ring: numbers and memories stored as remainders on several small prime 'rings', which makes some arithmetic exact and order-independent and lets a memory be found by its address instead of by searching. The repositories are the engines (exact ring arithmetic, ring memory, a shared-memory vector core), the agent tooling that runs a fleet of AI coding agents safely and cheaply, a from-scratch web browser engine, and the research papers with the scripts that produced every number. Each repository has a quick test you can run in minutes, and each claim it makes has a test you can re-run.
about.intermediate: Engines: armilla-astrolabe (carry-free residue-number-system arithmetic on CPUs: exact sums, sign/ReLU from the rings, an exact training step), omni-ring (vector-symbolic / hyperdimensional memory on rings with an AVX2 C kernel), vsa-core (shared-memory hypervector bus in C). Agents: talon (agent engine), tarsus (safety and tool-call repair), dock (one MCP front for many MCP servers), cost-savers (token reduction), agent-reliability-kit (routing, grounding, a done-gate), omnid (local embeddings and an MCP face). Browser: omni-render (rendering engine with integer layout and a JS runtime) and omni-ui (apps and a light browser on it). Research: omniring-research (the measured corpus, CC BY 4.0, with its harness). Licences: the engines and agent tools are PolyForm Small Business OR Noncommercial (free trial for evaluation); dock and omnid are Apache-2.0; the browser is MIT OR Apache-2.0; the corpus is CC BY 4.0.
about.advanced: Every repository carries DOSSIER.md (history, metrics, limits), PROVENANCE.md (sources, clean-room notes), TECHNICAL-DISCLOSURE.md where it discloses a method as dated prior art, and CITATION.cff with a Zenodo DOI. Claims are tied to evidence files committed in the repo; suite.json lists each claim with its verify command, the expected output, what passing means, how the number was obtained and its honest limits. Corrections are logged and applied as errata in the research corpus. Start from llms.txt for raw links to all of these.

repos.one_line: Carry-free residue-number-system engine on ordinary CPUs: exact integer arithmetic on coprime prime rings, with a ternary pull engine, an exact training step and RNS modular exponentiation.
repos.summary: A number is held as its remainders on many small prime rings, like beads on rods that never pass a carry. On top of that sit three old ideas, rebuilt for today's processors: The outer rings precompute answers; the centre pulls them straight into SIMD; a check ring verifies every result.

repos.one_line: Residue hyperdimensional computing engine: coprime-ring (CRT) memory with a check ring, resonator decode, two-faced ternary/phase hypervector slot, AVX2 C kernel, shards and a shared-memory bus.
repos.summary: `omni-ring` is a production-grade, zero-external-dependency (NumPy + standard library + AVX2 C-kernel) implementation of the OMNIRING Coprime Resonator Hyperdimensional Engine and the Two-Faced Polymorphic Bus with shared-memory (`/dev/shm`) IPC. Harnesses, result files and pre-registrations for Parts 3 and 4 are in [`experiments/`](experiments/). Parts 5–7 are in the research corpus ([omniring-research](https://github.com/SovRing-Labs/omniring-research), `docs/disclosures/`). Changes in this release: [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md).
repos.limits: A cue is mandatory for resonance; unguided decoding is seed-dependent and abstains when it fails. Resonant capacity ≈ 12 marks per slot at one cue (the exhaustive sift reads more). Superposition is finite: triangle buckets are safe to 256 facts; beyond that, truth must live in exact rows. Exact multi-hop lookups are ~250x faster in an indexed database (Part 2 §9).

repos.one_line: Ternary vector-symbolic kernel (10,240-dim, two bitplanes) and a POSIX shared-memory blackboard with a seqlock, AVX2 SIMD, phase kernel and trust classifier; C/C++ with a Python client.
repos.summary: Ternary Vector Symbolic Architecture kernel and shared-memory blackboard for the sovereign fleet. C/C++ with a POSIX `/dev/shm` bus, AVX2 SIMD, no external deps. A blackboard where 10 lanes (4 control heads + 6 workers) coordinate through a shared hypervector matrix rather than message passing. Each hypervector is 10,240 ternary dimensions `{-1, 0, +1}` stored as two bitplanes.
repos.limits: "Sub-nanosecond binding" was false (~35 ns). "67M ops/s" came from a degenerate benchmark. "Zero-token telemetry" is not how language models consume vectors — a projection head feeding a few slots is. Not built in 0.1.0: semantic search or routing over the bus; timing of a single published-slot read. The bus is single-machine shared memory; multi-machine use goes through omni-ring shards (Speculative at scale).

repos.summary: The research record behind OMNIRING, a memory that stores small structured records ("marks") in fixed-size high-dimensional vectors and reads them back by resonance. Its parts: These documents are the experiments and reviews that shaped the design. Most are pre-registered experiments: the pass/fail rule was written before any trial ran, and each document reports it word for word next to the result. Negative results (KILL) are published alongside positive ones.

census.last: VERDICT: KILL: the halo buys nothing. At M=32 Arm B's Wilson-99% lower bound (20.9%) does not exceed Arm A's point recall (33.3%), and Arm B does not match Arm A at half the iterations (medIt_B 5.0 vs medIt_A 2.0).

repos.one_line: Safe hands for tool-calling agents: batch tool execution with payload repair, a deterministic safety guard, kernel (Landlock) write confinement, human-only approval, audit trail and an MCP server. Linux only.
repos.summary: Tarsus (formerly *omnitool*) is the "hands" of an agent: one call carries a JSON batch of operations (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `patch`, `sql`, `glob`, `grep`, `fix_json`), which is repaired, validated, safety-checked and executed in parallel, sequentially or in dependency order, and answered with one structured result per operation. It is built for small, local, tool-calling models that routinely emit malformed payloads: it repairs what it can, refuses what it cannot, never runs half a batch its guard rejected — and since 0.2.0 the kernel itself confines what a bash command can write, and …
repos.limits: Preflight: an `operations` value that is a JSON *string* of an array is split into one-character bash ops; a top-level Python-dict string is rejected. The C++ interceptor's inference is not implemented; it answers with an explicit error by design. The advisory classifier does not discriminate destructive commands; it is advisory only.

Misrouted Dispatches: Simple keyword guesses route research tasks to fast code-generation models, or dispatch work to dead/flaky provider lanes. 2. Hallucinated Research: Research agents write convincing reports citing fictitious file paths or non-existent documentation. 3. Premature Task Completion: Agents claim success in …

repos.summary: `cost-savers` is the production token-reduction and cost-control layer developed for the Sovereign Raptor agent fleet. As autonomous agents operate over long sessions (50+ turns), uncurated context accumulation rapidly consumes model context windows, inflates per-turn inference costs, degrades attention accuracy, and leaks sensitive local file system paths or credentials to cloud providers. This package provides a modular set of agent harness plugins (compatible with the OpenCode plugin architecture) and supporting CLI tools:
repos.limits: The A/B covers short, read-only sessions on one free model; long sessions and other providers are untested. `cloud-pacer` deliberately slows requests. Plugins target OpenCode's plugin hooks; other agent runners need adapters.
